newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico closes six Gulf ports due to high winds.
newsitem.headline: Mexico closes six Gulf ports due to high winds.

text.p: Six Mexican Gulf ports were closed in Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche states as a cold front hit the area, causing high winds and rough seas, the Communications and Transportation Ministry said Wednesday.

The ports of Veracruz, Coatzacoalcos and Tuxpan in Veracruz state, Dos Bocas and Frontera in Tabasco state and Ciudad Carmen in Campeche were closed as of 1000 local time (11 EDT), the ministry added..

Dos Bocas is the second main crude terminal confimed closed due to the weather system in the area. Earlier, state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos said its Pajaritos crude port, which comes under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos, was also closed to shipping.
A spokeswoman at the port of Cayo Arcas in Campeche state said the terminal was also closed to shipping, making all three of Pemex's major Gulf shipping ports shut.
She said Cayo Arcas closed for outgoing vessels on Tuesday at 2000 local time (2100 EDT).
Sources at all three ports declined to estimate when the terminals might reopen, saying a renewal of activity would depend on how soon the weather system passes through the area.
The closure of Pemex's three main crude oil shipping ports halts new movements of outgoing vessels bound for the United States and Europe until weather conditions improve.
Oil shipping activity is expected to restart when the storm wanes, a Pemex spokeswoman said, adding that the company, as usual, would reschedule stalled shipments.
Gusts of up to 40 knots crossed the Gulf of Mexico to hit most severely on the Tabasco coast, the Communications and Transportation Ministry said in its update.

The storm front continued moving slowly south-southeast, lowering temperatures and also sending winds of up to 15 knots through southern Mexico, it added. Waves in the Gulf region were reported to be reaching 10 to 13 feet in height.
